Physiologically, the Stilt sandpiper exhibits a high basal metabolic rate consistent with its small body size and active foraging lifestyle. Field metabolic measurements during the chick-rearing period, when adults are provisioning young on the tundra, indicate sustained energy demands that are met by feeding on abundant dipteran larvae. The species' migration strategy, involving long-distance flights between Arctic breeding grounds and South American wintering areas, requires substantial fat reserves accumulated during the post-breeding period.
